novel.justification: After an operational outcome scale is fixed, bounded platform metrics are natural finite-population restrictions and permit design-based worst-case risk control.

A pathwise polynomial historical modulus represents persistent queues, inventories, and marketplace states without a distributed-lag equation; it deliberately places no restriction on the contemporaneous treatment contrast.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)=\{Y:\lvert Y_t(z_{1:t})\rvert\le B\text{ for all }t,z_{1:t},\text{ and }\lvert Y_t(z_{1:t})-Y_t(z'_{1:t})\rvert\le\sum_{\ell=1}^{t-1}C(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}\mathbf1\{z_{t-\ell}\ne z'_{t-\ell}\}\text{ whenever }z_t=z'_t,\ 1\le t\le T\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_T^{(0)}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_T^{(0)}=\{Y:\lvert Y_t(z_{1:t})\rvert\le B\text{ for all }t,z_{1:t},\ Y_t(z_{1:t})=Y_t(z'_{1:t})\text{ whenever }z_t=z'_t,\ 1\le t\le T\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal F_{T,m}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{T,m}=\{Y:\lvert Y_t(z_{1:t})\rvert\le B\text{ for all }t,z_{1:t},\ Y_t(z_{1:t})=Y_t(z'_{1:t})\text{ whenever }z_{(t-m)\vee1:t}=z'_{(t-m)\vee1:t},\ 1\le t\le T\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal D_T\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D_T=\{\pi:\pi_t(\cdot\mid W_{1:t-1},Y_{1:t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\text{ is a probability law on }\{0,1\},\ t=1,\ldots,T\}\).

statements.statement: Fix \(C>0\) and set \[C_0^\star=\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta_++1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C{\beta_-}.\] Uniformly over \(\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]\), \[\frac{B}{\sqrt{2T}}\le B2^{-(T-1)}\binom{T-1}{\lfloor(T-1)/2\rfloor}\le R_T(\beta;C).\] At \(T=1\), \[R_1(\beta;C)=B,\] attained from above by \(W_1\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\widehat\theta_1=(2W_1-1)Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\). For \(b\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), put \(r_b=b/(b+1)\), \(k_t=\min\{b,t-1\}\), \(\lambda_b=(b-1)/(b+1)\), \[V_{T,b}^{\dagger}=4\sum_{t=1}^T r_b^{-k_t}+8\sum_{h=1}^b\sum_{t=1}^{T-h}r_b^{h-k_{t+h}}+8\sum_{d=1}^{(T-b-1)_+}(T-b-d)\lambda_b^d,\] \[E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)=\frac2T\sum_{t=b+2}^T\min\left\{2B,\frac C2\sum_{\ell=b+1}^{t-1}(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}(1-\lambda_b^{\ell-b})\right\},\qquad U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)=\frac BT\sqrt{V_{T,b}^{\dagger}}+E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b),\] with empty inner sums equal to zero. Define the integrated finite oracle certificate \[\mathfrak U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}=\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ \min\left\{B,\min_{1\le b\le T}U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\right\},&T\ge2.\end{cases}\] Put \(b_\beta=\lceil T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\rceil\). Then \[R_T(\beta;C)\le\mathfrak U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}\le\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b_\beta),&T\ge2,\end{cases}\le\left[\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C\beta\right]T^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\le C_0^\star T^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.\] For \(T\ge2\), each Markov branch is the explicit beta-aware stationary Markov switchback and observed-data Horvitz--Thompson estimator of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:markov-washout-oracle-upper}\). The alternative \(B\) branch draws \(R\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) before outcomes, sets \(W_t=R\) for every \(t\), and uses \[\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}=(2R-1)T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t^{\mathrm{obs}}.\] Writing \(\mu_a=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t(\mathbf a_{1:t})\), its fixed-array risk is \((|\mu_0|+|\mu_1|)/2\le B\), and its exact worst-case risk is \(B\), attained by \(Y_t(z_{1:t})=B\). The finite minimum is attained, and one may select before assignment between the persistent homogeneous-path branch and the smallest minimizing Markov scale using only \(T,B,C,\beta\). The \(T=1\) value \(B\) comes from the explicit one-period procedure, not from an assertion that \(U_{1,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(1)=B\). The lower bound holds for every \(\pi\in\mathcal D_T\), including deterministic, history-dependent, and outcome-adaptive kernels without a positivity restriction. The Markov branches have \(\upsilon_{t,b,a}\ge1/(2q_b)>1/(2e)\), where \(q_b=(1+1/b)^b\), with unattained uniform infimum \(1/(2e)\). Their auxiliary homogeneous-history variance has exact worst-case value \(B^2V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\), whose sharp uniform coefficient is \(8e-4\). Their carryover terms are conditional, endpoint-aware expected replacement-error upper bounds obtained from the exact exposure-weight identity and the conditional mismatch formula, not exact biases or maximal-bias formulas. The auxiliary variance identity is not an exact estimator-risk identity. The lower and upper exponents differ; no matching lower bound at the upper exponent and no equality between the optimized certificate and oracle risk is claimed.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.} Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:positive-oracle-risk}\) gives, uniformly over \(\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]\),
\[
R_T(\beta;C)\ge B2^{-(T-1)}\binom{T-1}{\lfloor(T-1)/2\rfloor}\ge\frac{B}{\sqrt{2T}}>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Its supported no-carryover prior belongs to every \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\), and its likelihood argument covers every \(\pi\in\mathcal D_T\), including deterministic, history-dependent, and outcome-adaptive kernels without positivity.

We first establish the improved finite selector. Draw one random variable \(R\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) before outcomes, set \(W_t=R\) for every \(t\), and define
\[
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}=(2R-1)\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\tag{2}
\]
This outcome-independent rule is a member of \(\mathcal D_T\). For a fixed array, put
\[
\mu_a=\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t(\mathbf a_{1:t}),\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
By Definition~\(\mathrm{def:gate}\), \(\operatorname{GATE}_T(Y)=\mu_1-\mu_0\). If \(R=1\), then \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}=\mu_1\), so the absolute error is \(|\mu_0|\). If \(R=0\), then \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}=-\mu_0\), so the absolute error is \(|\mu_1|\). Consequently
\[
\mathbb E\left|\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}-\operatorname{GATE}_T(Y)\right|
=\frac{|\mu_0|+|\mu_1|}{2}
\le B,
\tag{3}
\]
where the inequality follows from Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:bounded-array}\). The constant array \(Y_t(z_{1:t})=B\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\): it is bounded and its historical differences vanish. For this array \(\mu_0=\mu_1=B\), and equality holds in \((3)\). Thus the exact worst-case risk of the persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin procedure is \(B\), for every \(T,C,\beta\). This calculation does not assert positivity for that branch.

At \(T=1\), the same construction is \(W_1\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) with \(\widehat\theta_1=(2W_1-1)Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \((3)\) gives risk at most \(B\). The lower bound in \((1)\) equals \(B\), proving
\[
R_1(\beta;C)=B.
\tag{4}
\]

Suppose \(T\ge2\). For every \(b\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:markov-washout-oracle-upper}\) constructs the stated stationary Markov switchback and observed-data Horvitz--Thompson estimator and proves
\[
\sup_{Y\in\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)}
\mathbb E_{\pi^{(b)}}\left|\widehat\vartheta_b-\operatorname{GATE}_T(Y)\right|
\le U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b).
\tag{5}
\]
Combining \((3)\) and \((5)\) yields
\[
R_T(\beta;C)
\le\min\left\{B,\min_{1\le b\le T}U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\right\}
=\mathfrak U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}.
\tag{6}
\]
The index set is finite, so the Markov minimum is attained. One may select before assignment between the persistent homogeneous branch and the smallest minimizing Markov scale using only \(T,B,C,\beta\). Together with \((4)\), this proves the finite upper certificate for every \(T\).

Put \(K=8e-4\), \(x=T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(b_\beta=\lceil x\rceil\). For \(T\ge2\), one has \(1<x<T\), hence \(b_\beta\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and
\[
\frac{b_\beta}{x}\le1+\frac1x\le1+2^{-1/(2\beta+1)},
\qquad b_\beta\ge x.
\tag{7}
\]
The final inequality of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:markov-washout-oracle-upper}\), together with \((T-b_\beta-1)_+/T\le1\), \((b_\beta+1)^{-\beta}\le b_\beta^{-\beta}\), and \((7)\), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b_\beta)
&\le\sqrt K\,B\sqrt{\frac{b_\beta}{T}}+\frac C\beta b_\beta^{-\beta}\\
&\le\left[\sqrt{K\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C\beta\right]T^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
At \(T=1\), the piecewise certificate is \(B\), and the coefficient in \((8)\) is larger than \(B\), so the same chain holds. Finally,
\[
2^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\le2^{-1/(2\beta_++1)},
\qquad \beta^{-1}\le\beta_-^{-1}.
\tag{9}
\]
Substituting \(K=8e-4\) into \((8)\) and applying \((9)\) gives the coefficient \(C_0^\star\).

The Markov exposure floor, the exact worst-case auxiliary variance \(B^2V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\), the sharp uniform coefficient \(8e-4\), and the exact conditional mismatch calculation all follow from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:markov-washout-oracle-upper}\). They apply only to the Markov branches. In particular, the conditional carryover term is an expected replacement-error bound rather than an exact bias or maximal error, and exactness of the auxiliary variance implies neither exact observed-data risk nor equality between the optimized certificate and oracle risk. Replacing the former \(2B\) selector branch by \((2)\) changes none of these facts and does not close the mismatch between the lower and upper exponents. \(\square\)
statements.justification: The theorem combines the policy-uniform hidden-counterfactual-sign floor, the exact \(B\)-risk persistent homogeneous-path selector, the exact Markov auxiliary variance, and the conditional replacement certificate.
statements.gap: The lower and upper exponents remain unmatched, so the exact growing-horizon oracle order is not identified.
statements.consumer: With known \(\beta\), compare the persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin procedure with the Markov certificates \(U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\) and select the smallest certified branch before assignment.

statements.statement: For every \(\beta\), \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(0)=\mathcal P_T^{(0)}\) literally: substituting \(C=0\) in the historical-envelope definition forces equality exactly for path pairs with \(z_t=z'_t\), while \(Y_t(1,z_{1:t-1})\) and \(Y_t(0,z'_{1:t-1})\) remain unrestricted apart from boundedness. Consequently \(R_T(\beta;0)=R_T^{(0)}\asymp_B T^{-1/2}\). The upper construction is independent \(\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment with the ordinary timewise positive-probability Horvitz--Thompson direct-effect contrast; a bounded fixed-array lower bound matches it.
statements.justification: This proposition identifies the literal zero-radius member of the same class and risk definition without deleting direct effects.
statements.gap: This is the required no-carryover sanity reduction, not a comparison against an external estimator.
statements.consumer: It verifies that unrestricted immediate treatment effects retain ordinary root-\(T\) randomization precision when historical carryover is absent.

statements.statement: Fix \(C>0\). For every \(m<T-1\), \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\cap\mathcal F_{T,m}\subsetneq\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\). Let \(a_m=\tfrac12\min\{B,C(2+m)^{-(1+\beta)}\}>0\) and set \(Y_t(z_{1:t})=a_mz_{t-m-1}\) for \(t\ge m+2\) and \(Y_t(z_{1:t})=0\) otherwise. This array is bounded, obeys the historical polynomial envelope, and is not in \(\mathcal F_{T,m}\). Moreover \(Y_t(z_{1:t})=\sum_{\ell=1}^{t-1}\gamma_\ell z_{t-\ell}\), with \(\gamma_\ell=C(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}/\{2\max[1,(C/B)\sum_{u=1}^{T-1}(1+u)^{-(1+\beta)}]\}\), is bounded, admissible, has positive effects at every lag, and lies outside every prespecified \(\mathcal F_{T,m}\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.} For the first witness,
\[
a_m=\frac12\min\{B,C(2+m)^{-(1+\beta)}\}>0.
\]
Thus \(a_m\le B/2\). If two histories with the same current treatment are compared at time \(t\), the corresponding outcomes can differ only through the lag-\((m+1)\) coordinate, and therefore
\[
\left|Y_t(z_{1:t})-Y_t(z'_{1:t})\right|
\le a_m\mathbf 1\{z_{t-m-1}\ne z'_{t-m-1}\}
\le C(2+m)^{-(1+\beta)}
\mathbf 1\{z_{t-m-1}\ne z'_{t-m-1}\}.
\]
This is one term of the required historical envelope. At \(t=m+2\), choose two histories that agree in coordinates \(2,\ldots,m+2\) and differ in coordinate one. They agree on \(z_{(t-m)\vee1:t}=z_{2:m+2}\), but their outcomes differ by \(a_m>0\). Hence this array is in \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\) and not in \(\mathcal F_{T,m}\).

For the second witness, put
\[
S=\sum_{u=1}^{T-1}(1+u)^{-(1+\beta)},
\qquad
D=2\max\{1,(C/B)S\}.
\]
Then \(\gamma_\ell=C(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}/D>0\), and
\[
0\le Y_t(z_{1:t})
\le\sum_{\ell=1}^{T-1}\gamma_\ell
=\frac{CS}{2\max\{1,(C/B)S\}}
\le\frac B2.
\]
For equal-current histories, the triangle inequality gives
\[
\left|Y_t(z_{1:t})-Y_t(z'_{1:t})\right|
\le\sum_{\ell=1}^{t-1}\gamma_\ell
\mathbf1\{z_{t-\ell}\ne z'_{t-\ell}\}
\le\sum_{\ell=1}^{t-1}C(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}
\mathbf1\{z_{t-\ell}\ne z'_{t-\ell}\},
\]
because \(D\ge2\). Thus the array is bounded and admissible. For every prespecified \(m<T-1\), the same two histories at \(t=m+2\) produce outcomes differing by \(\gamma_{m+1}>0\), so this array is not in \(\mathcal F_{T,m}\).

Finally, the zero array belongs to \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\cap\mathcal F_{T,m}\), whereas the first witness belongs to \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\) but not to \(\mathcal F_{T,m}\). Therefore
\[
\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C)\cap\mathcal F_{T,m}
\subsetneq\mathcal P_{T,\beta}(C).
\]
No common-design or minimax-optimality consequence is used or asserted. \(\square\)
statements.justification: The proposition makes the class relation with every prespecified finite-memory model literal using two explicit fixed arrays.
statements.gap: It is a structural scope statement only and carries no common-design or minimax-optimality consequence.
statements.consumer: A reader can verify whether a deployment lies in a finite-order intersection or requires the infinite-tail envelope.

statements.statement: For fixed \(C>0\) and \(\beta_-<\beta_+\), determine the joint status of (K1), a fixed-before-assignment endpoint-prior construction proving a policy-uniform two-class lower bound \(A_T(C)\ge g_T\) with \(g_T\to\infty\), and (K2), one common multiscale design and estimator, independent of the realized \(\beta\), proving \(A_T(C)=T^{o(1)}\); then determine the sharp asymptotic order of \(A_T(C)\). The two routes are not mutually exclusive; logarithmic divergence, for example, could satisfy both. Put \[C_0^\star=\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta_++1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C{\beta_-}.\] For \(b\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), define \(r_b=b/(b+1)\), \(k_t=\min\{b,t-1\}\), \(\lambda_b=(b-1)/(b+1)\), \[V_{T,b}^{\dagger}=4\sum_{t=1}^T r_b^{-k_t}+8\sum_{h=1}^b\sum_{t=1}^{T-h}r_b^{h-k_{t+h}}+8\sum_{d=1}^{(T-b-1)_+}(T-b-d)\lambda_b^d,\] \[E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)=\frac2T\sum_{t=b+2}^T\min\left\{2B,\frac C2\sum_{\ell=b+1}^{t-1}(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}(1-\lambda_b^{\ell-b})\right\},\qquad U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)=\frac BT\sqrt{V_{T,b}^{\dagger}}+E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b),\] with empty inner sums equal to zero. Put \(b_-=\lceil T^{1/(2\beta_-+1)}\rceil\) and define \[N_T^{\mathrm{fin}}=\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ U_{T,\beta_-}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b_-),&T\ge2,\end{cases}\qquad N_T^\star=\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ \min\left\{B,\min_{1\le b\le T}U_{T,\beta_-}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\right\},&T\ge2,\end{cases}\] and \[D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}=B2^{-(T-1)}\binom{T-1}{\lfloor(T-1)/2\rfloor}.\] The strongest currently certified common-design polynomial upper certificate is \[1\le A_T(C)\le\frac{N_T^\star}{D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}}\le\frac{N_T^{\mathrm{fin}}}{D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}}\le\frac{\sqrt2}{B}\left[\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta_-+1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C{\beta_-}\right]T^{1/(4\beta_-+2)}.\] At \(T=1\), \(N_1^\star=N_1^{\mathrm{fin}}=D_1^{\mathrm{bin}}=B\) and \(A_1(C)=1\), using the explicit fair-Bernoulli one-period procedure rather than an assertion that \(U_{1,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(1)=B\). For \(T\ge2\), the \(B\) branch draws \(R\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) before outcomes, sets \(W_t=R\), and uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}=(2R-1)T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Its fixed-array risk is \((|\mu_0|+|\mu_1|)/2\le B\), where \(\mu_a=T^{-1}\sum_tY_t(\mathbf a_{1:t})\), and the admissible constant array attains \(B\). The common selector chooses before assignment between this persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin branch and the smallest minimizing \(\beta_-\)-tuned Markov scale, independently of the realized \(\beta\). The ratios use the exact binomial Bayes lower bound as the oracle-risk denominator; they do not use the unknown exact oracle risk except at \(T=1\), and the certificate is not K2. The endpoint-specific coefficient is retained because \(\beta_-\) is known for this common design; it is not replaced by the larger \(\beta_+\)-uniform constant \(C_0^\star\). The certified two-class factor remains \(g_T=1\). The proved supported-prior lower obstructions are policy-uniform within their individual classes, but no policy-uniform two-class cross-law tradeoff has been derived. Neither a divergent \(g_T\), a \(T^{o(1)}\) common multiscale procedure, a matching oracle rate, nor the sharp order has been proved; K1 and K2 remain logically compatible.
statements.justification: The \(B\)-elbow improves the finite common-design numerator but does not couple the rough and smooth supported-prior obstructions across decay classes.
statements.gap: A divergent two-class factor, a common \(T^{o(1)}\) multiscale procedure, a matching oracle rate, and the sharp order of \(A_T(C)\) remain open.
statements.consumer: A resolution would quantify the growing-horizon value of knowing the decay index beyond the exact finite selector and endpoint-specific polynomial certificate.

sampling_model.design: There is one experimental unit and horizon \(T\). The assignment path is generated by a known sequential kernel, and the admissible class includes deterministic and outcome-adaptive rules. Potential outcomes are a fixed bounded array, and assignment is the only randomness. Constructive upper bounds select before assignment either the persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin rule \(W_t=R\) for all \(t\), or an outcome-independent stationary symmetric Markov chain that switches with probability \(1/(b+1)\). The beta-aware selector may use \(\beta\); the common selector uses only \(\beta_-\).
sampling_model.units: One fixed unit over the experiment horizon.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignment, assigned at every time through the horizon.
sampling_model.overlap: Oracle competitors need not satisfy positivity. Each Markov estimator has \(\upsilon_{t,b,a}=\tfrac12\{b/(b+1)\}^{k_t}\ge1/(2q_b)>1/(2e)\), with unattained uniform infimum \(1/(2e)\). No positivity claim is made for the persistent homogeneous-path branch.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no outcome noise or superpopulation nuisance; expectations integrate only assignment randomization for the fixed array.

estimand_functional: For \(C>0\), let \[C_0^\star=\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta_++1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C{\beta_-}.\] For \(b\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), put \(r_b=b/(b+1)\), \(k_t=\min\{b,t-1\}\), \(q_b=(1+1/b)^b\), and \(\lambda_b=(b-1)/(b+1)\), and define \[V_{T,b}^{\dagger}=4\sum_{t=1}^T r_b^{-k_t}+8\sum_{h=1}^b\sum_{t=1}^{T-h}r_b^{h-k_{t+h}}+8\sum_{d=1}^{(T-b-1)_+}(T-b-d)\lambda_b^d,\] \[E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)=\frac2T\sum_{t=b+2}^T\min\left\{2B,\frac C2\sum_{\ell=b+1}^{t-1}(1+\ell)^{-(1+\beta)}(1-\lambda_b^{\ell-b})\right\},\qquad U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)=\frac BT\sqrt{V_{T,b}^{\dagger}}+E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b),\] with empty inner sums equal to zero. The Markov branch at scale \(b\) has \[\upsilon_{t,b,a}=\frac12r_b^{k_t}\ge\frac{1}{2q_b}>\frac{1}{2e},\] and the unattained uniform infimum over admissible \(T,b,t,a\) is \(1/(2e)\). For \(t\ge b+2\), \(b+1\le\ell\le t-1\), and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \[\Pr_{\pi^{(b)}}(W_{t-\ell}\ne a\mid H_{t,b,a}=1)=\frac{1-\lambda_b^{\ell-b}}2.\] Its exact worst-case auxiliary homogeneous-history variance is \(B^2V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\), and \[V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\le4q_bT+8Tb(q_b-1)+4(T-b)(b-1)< (8e-4)Tb,\] with \[\lim_{b\to\infty}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{V_{T,b}^{\dagger}}{Tb}=8e-4.\] Thus \(8e-4\) is the optimal uniform coefficient for this auxiliary variance inequality. If \(b_\beta=\lceil T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\rceil\), define \[\mathfrak U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}=\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ \min\left\{B,\min_{1\le b\le T}U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\right\},&T\ge2.\end{cases}\] The competing \(B\) branch draws \(R\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) before outcomes, sets \(W_t=R\) for every \(t\), and uses \[\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{hom}}=(2R-1)T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t^{\mathrm{obs}}.\] For \(\mu_a=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t(\mathbf a_{1:t})\), its fixed-array risk is \((|\mu_0|+|\mu_1|)/2\le B\); the constant admissible array \(Y_t(\cdot)=B\) attains equality, so its exact worst-case risk is \(B\). The beta-aware finite selector chooses before assignment between this persistent branch and the smallest minimizing Markov scale. Then \[\frac{B}{\sqrt{2T}}\le B2^{-(T-1)}\binom{T-1}{\lfloor(T-1)/2\rfloor}\le R_T(\beta;C)\le\mathfrak U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}\le\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b_\beta),&T\ge2,\end{cases}\le\left[\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C\beta\right]T^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\le C_0^\star T^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.\] At \(T=1\), \(R_1(\beta;C)=B\), supplied by the explicit fair-Bernoulli one-period procedure rather than by \(U_{1,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(1)\). For \(b_-=\lceil T^{1/(2\beta_-+1)}\rceil\), define \[N_T^{\mathrm{fin}}=\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ U_{T,\beta_-}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b_-),&T\ge2,\end{cases}\qquad N_T^\star=\begin{cases}B,&T=1,\\ \min\left\{B,\min_{1\le b\le T}U_{T,\beta_-}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\right\},&T\ge2,\end{cases}\] The \(B\) branch in \(N_T^\star\) is the same exact-risk persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin procedure. The alternative Markov branch is tuned only to the known endpoint \(\beta_-\), so the common selector is independent of the realized \(\beta\). Define \[D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}=B2^{-(T-1)}\binom{T-1}{\lfloor(T-1)/2\rfloor}.\] Then \[1\le A_T(C)\le\frac{N_T^\star}{D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}}\le\frac{N_T^{\mathrm{fin}}}{D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}}\le\frac{\sqrt2}{B}\left[\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta_-+1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C{\beta_-}\right]T^{1/(4\beta_-+2)}.\] At \(T=1\), \(N_1^\star=N_1^{\mathrm{fin}}=D_1^{\mathrm{bin}}=B\) and \(A_1(C)=1\). The auxiliary variance exactness is not exact estimator-risk, bias, carryover-error, or oracle-risk exactness. The conditional carryover term is an expected replacement-error upper bound, not an exact bias or maximal error. The adaptation ratios use the exact binomial Bayes lower bound as an oracle-risk denominator; they do not use the unknown exact oracle risk except at \(T=1\). The last coefficient is endpoint-specific and is not replaced by the larger \(\beta_+\)-uniform constant \(C_0^\star\)

Page 1, abstract and introduction, model treatment and control as unknown reusable-state Markov chains and give an adaptive online design that is consistent and asymptotically efficient under that stochastic model.

The accepted-bank theorem gives a matched Chebyshev--Lobatto minimax frontier for choosing treated-fraction rollout nodes under a network polynomial-outcome model and a total-variation variance envelope; it does not analyze one-unit temporal carryover, sequential cadence, or unknown-decay adaptation.

tldr: In a one-unit, fixed-array switchback experiment with assignment as the only randomness, the stationary Markov washout rule at scale \(b\) has exact worst-case auxiliary homogeneous-history variance \(B^2V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\), sharp uniform coefficient \(8e-4\), and exposure floor with unattained infimum \(1/(2e)\). For \(t\ge b+2\), \(b+1\le\ell\le t-1\), and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), reversibility gives \(\Pr_{\pi^{(b)}}(W_{t-\ell}\ne a\mid H_{t,b,a}=1)=(1-\lambda_b^{\ell-b})/2\), yielding the computable replacement certificate \(E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\), risk bound \(U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\), and oracle ceiling exponent \(\beta/(2\beta+1)\). A second fixed-before-assignment branch draws one fair coin and holds that arm for the entire horizon; its exact worst-case risk is \(B\). It sharpens both beta-aware and common finite selectors from a \(2B\) elbow to a \(B\) elbow. The exact identities \(R_1(\beta;C)=B\) and \(A_1(C)=1\) persist. For growing horizons, the exact oracle order and the unknown-decay adaptation dichotomy remain open.

project_justification.gap: Known-order switchback results do not pose the min-over-designs, max-over-the-pair \((Y,\beta)\) problem over all sequential outcome-adaptive kernels. The supported priors give policy-uniform lower obstructions within individual classes but not the two-class cross-law tradeoff required for divergent adaptation. The exact \(B\)-risk persistent branch tightens the finite numerator selector, yet no common \(T^{o(1)}\) multiscale procedure, matching oracle lower rate, or sharp order of \(A_T(C)\) is known.
project_justification.niche: The note indexes nested fixed-array historical-envelope classes directly by an unknown polynomial decay exponent, without a distributed-lag equation, outcome noise, or a superpopulation, and permits fully sequential assignment. It supplies evaluable finite design guarantees, including an exact \(B\)-risk persistent homogeneous-path selector branch, and isolates why within-class lower obstructions do not yet yield an across-class adaptation theorem.
project_justification.fill: For every washout scale \(b\), the note proves the exact worst-case auxiliary homogeneous-history variance \(B^2V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\), its sharp uniform coefficient \(8e-4\), and the exact conditional pre-window mismatch identity on the domain \(t\ge b+2\), \(b+1\le\ell\le t-1\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\). These yield \(U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\) and the beta-aware ceiling coefficient \(\sqrt{(8e-4)(1+2^{-1/(2\beta+1)})}\,B+C/\beta\). In addition, the persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin procedure has fixed-array risk \((|\mu_0|+|\mu_1|)/2\le B\) and exact worst-case risk \(B\), so finite beta-aware and common selectors use a \(B\) elbow. The exact binomial oracle-risk floor, the Markov exposure floor, and the one-period identities remain unchanged. The K1/K2 dichotomy is still the disclosed residual.

related_work:
Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao study switchback experiments under a known finite carryover order, and Yu, Ma, and Liu optimize under a known carryover specification. Zeng and coauthors allow outcome-history-adaptive sequential rerandomization under no or first-order carryover; Xiong, Chin, and Taylor analyze modeled bias--variance tradeoffs; Hu and Wager use geometric mixing; and Glynn, Johari, and Rasouli study adaptive reusable-state Markov models. None poses one common design-estimator pair against the nested pair \((Y,\beta)\) in the fixed-array historical-envelope model. The present theorem's finite selector now includes an exact \(B\)-risk persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin branch, but this finite improvement does not resolve the unknown-decay adaptation problem.

The closest accepted-bank experimental-design minimax result is \(\texttt{exp\_rollout\_chebyshev\_minimax\_tv\_envelope\_rollout\_design/thm:chebyshev-minimax}\). It chooses treated-fraction nodes for a many-unit network rollout whose mean is a polynomial and proves a matched Chebyshev--Lobatto frontier under a total-variation variance envelope. That theorem does not subsume the present one-unit result: it has no temporal potential-outcome history, Markov cadence, carryover replacement error, fully sequential policy class, or unknown decay index. Conversely, the present theorem does not optimize rollout-node geometry, use polynomial extrapolation, or prove a matched network-rollout minimax frontier.
interpretation: When \(\beta\) is known, compute \(U_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\) over all integer scales and compare its minimum with \(B\). Select before assignment either the persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin procedure or the smallest minimizing Markov washout scale. The persistent branch has exact worst-case risk \(B\); the Markov variance is exact only for the auxiliary homogeneous-history process, and its carryover term is an expected replacement-error upper bound. The scale \(b_\beta=\lceil T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\rceil\) gives the displayed power-rate certificate. At \(T=1\), the persistent rule reduces to the fair-Bernoulli procedure and yields \(R_1(\beta;C)=B\) and \(A_1(C)=1\). Without knowing \(\beta\), tune the Markov candidate to \(\beta_-\) and compare it with the same persistent branch; this controls every nested class but yields only the displayed polynomial oracle ratio.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(B\) risk is exact only for the persistent selector branch; it is not the oracle risk except at \(T=1\). The identity \(B^2V_{T,b}^{\dagger}\) concerns the auxiliary homogeneous-history variance, not the observed-data estimator's exact risk. The conditional quantity \(E_{T,\beta}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\) retains its internal per-time cap \(2B\) and is a capped expected replacement-error upper bound, not exact bias or maximal carryover error. The exact binomial expression is an oracle-risk lower bound, not oracle risk itself except at \(T=1\). The beta-aware upper exponent remains unmatched by the universal \(1/2\) lower exponent. Markov positivity applies only to the Markov branches. The \(B\)-elbow improvement supplies neither the missing two-class complementarity inequality nor a decay-agnostic \(T^{o(1)}\) multiscale selector.
honest_scope: The paper proves computable finite design-risk upper bounds, the exact \(B\)-risk persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin branch, the exact worst-case auxiliary homogeneous-history variance for the Markov construction, the sharp uniform auxiliary-variance coefficient \(8e-4\), the Markov-family exposure floor \(1/(2e)\), the exact conditional pre-window mismatch probability, capped endpoint-aware conditional replacement control, the beta-aware ceiling rate, exact identities \(R_1(\beta;C)=B\) and \(A_1(C)=1\), finite selectors with a \(B\) elbow, an oracle bracket with unmatched exponents, and an endpoint-specific common-design polynomial certificate. It does not prove a matching growing-horizon oracle rate, divergent adaptation cost, a subpolynomial common procedure, a sharp order of \(A_T(C)\), or that adaptation is never free. K1 and K2 remain jointly open and logically compatible.
